newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai 1996 non-oil trade rose to 82.1 bln dirhams.
newsitem.headline: Dubai 1996 non-oil trade rose to 82.1 bln dirhams.

text.p: The value of Dubai's non-oil foreign trade rose to 82.1 billion dirhams ($22.3 billion) in 1996, up 13.4 percent from 72.4 billion dirhams in 1995, Dubai's Department of Economic Development said.
Imports to Dubai, the trading hub of the United Arab Emirates, increased to 61.8 billion dirhams in 1996, up 13.1 percent on the previous year, it said in a report obtained by Reuters on Sunday.
Non-oil exports declined by 10.1 percent in 1996 to 4.2 billion dirhams while re-exports firmed to 16.1 billion, up 23.3 percent from 1995.
The report said durable consumer goods represented the largest single group among imports, accounting for 42.9 percent of total import value in 1996.

The United States was Dubai's top supplier, with imports rising 55.4 percent from the previous year to 6.9 billion dirhams. Vehicles and machinery formed the largest group of U.S. exports to the emirate.
China came second, exporting goods to Dubai worth 6.6 billion dirhams. Textiles and textile products were the largest group of Chinese imports in Dubai.
Japan was the third largest supplier with exports of 10.3 billion dirhams in 1996, up 35.7 percent from 1995. Vehicles and machinery represented the largest chunk of Japanese imports.
The report attributed the drop in Dubai's exports to an 86.4 percent decline in the value of capital goods exports.
Dubai exported goods to 129 countries in 1996, with Japan, Taiwan and the United States the top three destinations.

Re-exports, led by durable consumer goods, increased by 23.3 percent to reach 16.1 billion dirhams in 1996. Iran was the top re-export destination, amounting to 2.9 billion dirhams. Machinery and electronics were the main re-exported goods.
India was Dubai's second largest re-export destination, with pearls, precious stones and metals accounting for 45 percent re-exports to India.
Saudi Arabia was the third largest re-export destination, importing mostly textiles and related products.
